pr.title: Print a Windows home path with a tilde (windows-portability.md §7.2)
pr.head: 6d640adc9bec55e2bb1aeded43cd1cdbd52114c2

summary: field export builds labels and copies the results to ~/Desktop, or to the folder --to names, and prints one line per file saying where it landed. To keep that line short, it prints a path under your home folder with ~ in place of the home folder, through homeRelative in src/commands/export.ts.

On Windows that shortening never happened. homeRelative checked for the home path followed by /, but Windows paths use \, so every export printed its full C:\Users\… path. The Windows portability plan recorded this in its list of standalone defects (windows-portability.md §7.2).

This pull request gives homeRelative a separator parameter that defaults to path.sep, the platform's separator. A Windows path under the profile now prints as ~\Desktop\…, a sibling folder such as C:\Users\justinx is still not treated as home, and macOS and Linux keep /. The plan marks the item done.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first head, ae05c15, also ported the sclang lookup. The author removed that in 6d640ad and left it to #186, so the two pull requests no longer overlap except in the plan file, where they edit different items.
  • The review of 6d640ad requests changes with one open finding: the existing homeRelative test fails on the Windows CI job, because its POSIX assertions now take the Windows default separator there.
  • The linux CI job passes. The windows job's other 12 failures also fail on main.

cards.title: Left for later
cards.html:
• On a OneDrive-redirected profile, the Desktop you see lives under OneDrive\Desktop, not where defaultExportDir() writes. The plan calls this a cosmetic wart, and it stays.
  • No Windows machine has run field export with this change. The unit test is the only coverage.

groups.title: Shortening the home folder with the platform's separator
groups.kicker: How the export line decides whether a path is under your home folder
intro: homeRelative(path, home, separator) returns path with ~ in place of home when the path is the home folder itself or sits inside it. A path is inside the home folder only when it starts with the home path followed by a separator, so /Users/justinx never becomes ~x.

The change makes that separator a parameter. Its default is path.sep, which is / on macOS and Linux and \ on Windows, so the only caller, the export line in src/cli.ts, gets the right rule on each platform without passing anything.

checks.text: The default export folder is join(homedir(), 'Desktop'), so on Windows it always starts with the home path and a \. A --to folder that you type in another case, such as c:\users\me\Music, still prints in full, because the comparison is case-sensitive. That matches main and is cosmetic.

files.note: Adds the separator parameter, defaulting to path.sep, and uses it in the prefix check.

checks.text: On macOS, mocking node:path's sep to \ made homeRelative('C:\\Users\\justin\\Desktop\\x.wav', 'C:\\Users\\justin') return ~\Desktop\x.wav with the default separator, as a Windows host would.

files.note: Adds two Windows cases that pass \ explicitly: a file under the home folder, and a sibling folder that is not home.

checks.text: The existing POSIX assertions in this test, from line 184, leave the separator out, so on a Windows host they get \. The windows CI job fails abbreviates $HOME and only $HOME because homeRelative('/Users/justin/Desktop/creek-mix-main-v1.wav', '/Users/justin') comes back unchanged. Passing '/' in those assertions, as the Windows ones pass '\\', makes the test mean the same thing on every host.

groups.title: The plan records the item as done
groups.kicker: The Windows portability plan's list of standalone defects
intro: windows-portability.md §7.2 lists defects that the Windows sweep found outside any planned chunk. Each item stays in the list as a record, and a fixed one gains a dated Done note. This pull request adds that note to the homeRelative item and leaves the plan's status at in-progress.
